summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with dilated cardiomyopathy, chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of heavy alcohol use, was admitted after being punched in the chest and reporting his implantable defibrillator had fired. Device interrogation showed no shocks were delivered. He was intoxicated with an ethanol level of 313 and exhibited signs of alcohol withdrawal, managed with diazepam and supportive vitamins. His persistent tachycardia was controlled with metoprolol, and elevated liver enzymes and lipase normalized with supportive care. He reported chronic nausea and vomiting, likely related to alcohol and possible opioid use, and expressed a strong desire for rehabilitation. He stabilized, withdrawal symptoms resolved, and he was discharged to an extended care facility for alcohol treatment with updated medications and follow-up plans.
problems: Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
